en: a. not able to speak (an offensive use); (informal) stupid; silent or not willing to speak; (of a machine) not able to work on its own
ex: She stood there dumb with shock when she heard the news.
她聽到消息時震驚得說不出話。

en: a small piece of dough, often filled with meat or vegetables and boiled, steamed or fried; (UK) a ball of dough cooked in a stew
ex: We made dumplings for the Lunar New Year.
我們為農曆新年包了水餃。

en: a. wanting very much to do or have something; full of enthusiasm and interest
ex: The students were eager to start the experiment.
學生們迫不及待想開始實驗。

en: to correct and improve a piece of writing; to prepare a film, tape or recording by cutting and arranging it; to change a computer file; to be in charge of a publication
ex: She edited the video before posting it online.
她剪輯完影片才上傳到網路。

en: to teach someone, especially at a school or college; to give someone information about something so that they understand it better
ex: Parents should educate their children about road safety.
父母應該教導孩子交通安全。

en: a. relating to education; providing knowledge or learning; helping people to learn something
ex: The museum offers many educational programs for children.
博物館為孩子提供許多教育活動。

en: a. working well and quickly without wasting time or energy; (of a person) good at organizing work; (of a machine) using little power
ex: The new system is much more efficient than the old one.
新系統比舊系統有效率得多。

en: a. (of a person) old, especially in a way that is not strong; (the elderly) old people considered as a group
ex: The elderly man crossed the road slowly with a cane.
那位老先生拄著拐杖慢慢過馬路。

en: n. a form of energy that is used to produce light and heat, and to make machines work; the supply of this energy; (in a person's feelings) great excitement
ex: The storm cut off the electricity in the whole town.
暴風雨讓整個小鎮停電。

en: n. a basic part of something; a simple substance that cannot be divided into smaller substances, such as gold or oxygen; a small amount of a quality; a part of an electrical device that gives out heat
ex: Trust is an important element in any relationship.
信任是任何關係中重要的要素。

en: n. an unexpected and dangerous situation that needs immediate action; a. used for dealing with sudden dangerous situations
ex: Call the emergency number if someone is badly hurt.
如果有人受重傷，請撥緊急電話。

en: a. relating to feelings; showing strong feelings; (of a situation) making people feel strong emotions
ex: She became emotional when she saw her old friends again.
她再次見到老朋友時情緒激動。

en: a man who rules an empire or a group of countries; the title of the leader of a country such as Japan or ancient China
ex: The emperor ruled the country for over fifty years.
那位皇帝統治這個國家超過五十年。

en: v. to take part in an activity; to employ someone; to attract and keep someone's attention; to start fighting; (be engaged) to have formally agreed to marry; (engagement) a formal agreement to marry
ex: The company plans to engage more workers next year.
公司計畫明年僱用更多員工。

en: n. a feeling of wanting what someone else has; v. to feel unhappy because someone has something you want; to wish that you had what someone else has
ex: Everyone envied her for her beautiful voice.
大家都羨慕她美妙的歌聲。

en: v. to give something and receive something in return; to change money from one currency to another; n. the act of exchanging; a place where stocks are traded; a telephone center
ex: We exchanged phone numbers before saying goodbye.
我們在道別前交換了電話號碼。

en: n. a belief that something will happen; a strong belief that someone will do well or achieve something; what is expected
ex: The movie did not live up to our expectations.
這部電影沒有達到我們的期待。

en: n. a scientific test to find out what happens or to prove an idea; a trial of a new idea or way of doing something; v. to do a scientific test; to try something new to see if it works
ex: The students carried out an experiment in the chemistry lab.
學生們在化學實驗室進行了一項實驗。

en: v. to burst with a loud noise; to suddenly show strong feeling, especially anger; to increase very quickly; to prove that something is not true
ex: The bomb exploded in the middle of the night.
炸彈在半夜爆炸了。

en: v. to sell goods to another country; to send information from one computer program to another; n. a product that is sold to another country; the business of selling goods to other countries
ex: Taiwan exports a lot of electronic products.
台灣出口大量電子產品。

en: a. showing what you think or feel clearly; showing feeling or meaning in a clear and effective way; (of a face or voice) showing a lot of emotion
ex: She has a very expressive face that shows every emotion.
她的臉上表情豐富，每種情緒都看得出來。

en: a. very great in degree; far from what is usual or normal; n. the furthest possible point; a thing or situation that is as bad or as good as can be
ex: Be careful; the weather is extremely cold in winter.
小心，這裡冬天的天氣極度寒冷。

en: a. weak and not clear; (of a person) feeling weak and likely to fall; (of a hope or chance) very small; v. to suddenly become unconscious for a short time; n. a sudden loss of consciousness
ex: I could hear a faint sound coming from the next room.
我聽到隔壁房間傳來微弱的聲音。

en: adv. to a reasonable degree but not very; in a way that is right and equal; in a clear and honest way; completely (informal)
ex: The test was fairly easy, so most students passed.
這次考試相當簡單，所以大部分學生都及格了。

en: n. an imaginary small creature with magic powers, usually in the shape of a small person with wings; a. relating to fairies; very delicate and beautiful
ex: The children believed that a fairy lived in the garden.
孩子們相信花園裡住著一位仙子。

en: n. strong belief or trust in someone or something; a religion; loyalty to a person or promise; (in bad faith / good faith) the way someone behaves
ex: I have great faith in your ability to solve this problem.
我對你解決這個問題的能力很有信心。

en: a. not real, but made to look like the real thing; n. a copy of something valuable that is intended to look real; v. to pretend to have a feeling or illness; to make a copy of something in order to deceive people
ex: The police found a lot of fake money in the shop.
警方在店裡找到大量偽鈔。
ph: fake it till you make it

en: a. decorated and expensive; unusual and complicated; (of a price) very high; n. a liking for something; the power to imagine; v. to like something; to imagine something; (informal) to find someone sexually attractive
ex: They had dinner at a fancy restaurant to celebrate.
他們在一間高級餐廳吃晚餐慶祝。

en: n. the money you pay to travel by bus, train, taxi or plane; a passenger in a taxi; food that is provided; v. to progress or manage in a particular way
ex: The bus fare to the airport is ten dollars.
到機場的公車票價是十美元。

en: n. one of the light, soft things that cover a bird's body; v. to grow feathers; to cover with feathers; (in rowing) to turn the oar flat after pulling
ex: The bird lost a few feathers in the fight.
那隻鳥在打鬥中掉了幾根羽毛。

en: n. a person who fights, especially in a war or in sports like boxing; a fast military plane used for attacking other aircraft; a person who does not give up easily
ex: The firefighters fought bravely like true fighters.
消防員像真正的鬥士一樣勇敢奮戰。

en: n. a small container filled with explosive powder that makes bright colors and loud noises when it burns; (fireworks) a show of these; (informal) a sudden angry argument
ex: We watched the fireworks on New Year's Eve.
我們在跨年夜看了煙火。

en: n. a hand with the fingers curled in tightly, ready to hit someone; v. to hit someone with your fist; to close your hand tightly
ex: He shook his fist angrily at the driver.
他生氣地對司機揮舞拳頭。

en: n. a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is on fire; a strong feeling; v. to burn with a bright flame; to suddenly become angry; (informal) to criticize someone online in an angry way
ex: The flame of the candle flickered in the wind.
蠟燭的火焰在風中搖曳。

en: n. the taste of food or drink; a particular quality or feeling in something; v. to add something to food to give it a particular taste
ex: The ice cream comes in many different flavors.
這種冰淇淋有很多不同口味。

en: v. to stay on or near the surface of a liquid without sinking; to move slowly through the air or water; to offer an idea for discussion; (of a currency) to be allowed to change value freely; n. a light object that stays on the surface of water; a decorated truck in a parade
ex: The leaves floated down the river.
樹葉順著河水漂流而下。

en: n. a large amount of water covering an area that is usually dry; a very large number of things coming at the same time; v. to cover an area with water; to give or send someone too many things at once
ex: Heavy rain caused a flood in the lowlands.
大雨在低窪地區造成水災。

en: v. to bend something so that one part lies on top of another; to close something by bending it; (of a business) to fail; n. a line made in paper or cloth when it is bent; a small area of land enclosed for sheep
ex: She folded the letter and put it in the envelope.
她把信摺好放進信封。

en: n. a person who believes in or supports a person, a belief or a religion; a person who is on a social media site and follows another person's posts
ex: The singer has millions of followers on social media.
那位歌手在社群媒體上有數百萬名追蹤者。

en: a. liking someone or something very much; showing love and care; (be fond of) to like someone or something; (of a hope or belief) foolish or unlikely to come true
ex: She is very fond of her grandmother.
她非常喜歡她的奶奶。
